newsitem.title: GERMANY: Credit card use booming in Germany - report.
newsitem.headline: Credit card use booming in Germany - report.

text.p: Credit card use is rising strongly in Germany, with holders of the market-leading Eurocard up 16 percent at 7.9 million in 1996, processing group GZS (Gesellschaft fuer Zahlungssysteme) said on Thursday.

Noting that the recent vogue for branchless banking had boosted the card industry's cause, GZS managing director Laurenz Kohlleppel predicted German credit card holders would number 17 million by the year 2000, up from 13.6 million today.
Taking into account regular debit cards and cheque cards as well as credit cards, there were now 70 million cards in circulation in this traditionally cash-focused society.
Eurocard remains Germany's biggest seller with a 59 percent market share, followed by Visa with 30 percent, American Express with nine percent and Diners Club with two percent.

Transactions using Eurocard, a Europay product affiliated to MasterCard, amounted to 185.5 million in 1996, an 8.8 percent jump, and turnover rose 7.4 percent to 31 million marks ($18.9 million) from 28.9 million, GZS reported.
Most transactions took place within Germany itself and the average purchase size dropped to 165 marks from 168 marks.

Meanwhile the number of German firms with Eurocard contracts rose by 1.4 percent to 310,700, despite declines that included a 3.9 percent drop in the restaurant sector and a 2.8 percent drop among hotels, which GZS blamed on mergers.
Eurocard has three million acceptance points in Europe and 31.1 million worldwide.
